subject.title: feat(browser): add secure per-tab copilot panel

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose browser run bindings through the shared plugin tool context, and if so what typed, documented compatibility contract should plugins rely on?
rationale: The field changes a shared plugin-facing context and creates a lasting capability boundary; code review alone cannot select the intended public contract or its future compatibility policy.

options.title: Approve a typed browser binding contract
options.body: Keep the capability, replace the opaque record with a narrow documented type, and add compatibility and ownership tests.

options.title: Keep bindings browser-private
options.body: Move the binding transport behind the browser plugin/runtime seam so unrelated plugin tool factories do not receive a new generic API.

options.title: Pause for API design
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers decide whether general run-bound capabilities are a supported plugin API direction.

recommendation.title: Approve a typed browser binding contract
recommendation.body: Keep the capability, replace the opaque record with a narrow documented type, and add compatibility and ownership tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The related side-panel proposal established the feature direction and its stated follow-up is explicitly about adopting these contracts.
